title: The Overcoat
text:
Akaky Akakievich was a humble copying clerk in a government department in St. Petersburg. He loved copying and asked for nothing else. His colleagues mocked him and he barely noticed. His one problem was his overcoat, which had worn so thin that the bitter wind went straight through it. The tailor Petrovich declared it beyond repair. A new coat would cost about eighty rubles.

For months Akaky saved. He gave up his evening tea, did without candles and walked on tiptoe to spare his boots. At last the new coat was made, with a cat fur collar, and he wore it to the office as if it were a festival. That same night, crossing a dark square on his way home from a party, he was attacked by thieves who stripped the coat from his back.

The police were useless. Someone advised him to seek help from a certain Important Person, a man recently promoted who loved to show his authority. Akaky came at a moment when the Important Person had an old friend visiting and wanted to impress him. Instead of listening, he shouted at the clerk for his impertinence in coming directly to him, stamping his foot until Akaky nearly fainted.

Akaky went home through a blizzard, caught a fever and died within days. Afterward, the city was haunted by a ghost who pulled the coats off passersby, until one night he seized the Important Person's own coat.
lesson: To someone with little power, a moment of your attention can matter enormously. Never use a person in need as an audience for your own importance.
people: Akaky Akakievich, the Important Person, Petrovich the tailor
